About SINGU

At SINGU, we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business.

 

Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide, supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started.

 

Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus.

 

If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation.

About the Role

You'll own a significant slice of the SINGU product suite: space management and Soft FM services – cleaning standards, portering, and catering – used every day primarily across the UK healthcare market. Product-market fit is established and thousands of users depend on these products daily. What the portfolio needs now is strategic direction and taking them to their next level of growth.

You'll do that through a team of four Product Managers who are domain experts in the products they run. This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll stay close to customer problems yourself, you'll raise the bar on how the team discovers and validates work, and you'll have real autonomy to decide what's worth building – and to prove it works.

SINGU group grows both organically and through acquisition, and several of these products arrived with the companies that built them. You'll shape the strategy for bringing them into one coherent ecosystem and lead your team through that change. If you enjoy taking a set of good but separate products and making them add up to something bigger, that is the interesting part of this job.

You'll partner closely with Sales, Engineering, and Product colleagues across the SINGU Group so your portfolio drives revenue and solves real problems across the European FM market. AI is a must-have lever in our industry rather than a talking point: you'll be applying it where it measurably improves how our customers run their estates.

This is a remote position with periodic travel to London and Kraków – roughly every two to four weeks.

Role Scope

People Leadership & Team Development:

  • Manage and develop the Product Managers within the product team.

  • Own the full management lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, feedback, coaching, performance evaluations, promotions, and exits.

  • Foster a high-performing product culture based on customer empathy, data-driven decision-making, and outcome orientation.

You also grow the team by hiring strong engineers, giving direct and timely feedback, running a fair performance process, and helping people grow in ways that compound over time.

Who Will Thrive in This Role?

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

The role

We're hiring a Legal Engineer to help build out privacy and compliance as a brand new product vertical for Wordsmith, from the ground up.

This role spans privacy and compliance more generally - building products for customers, supporting pre-sales, and creating the global AI tools that power them. Its centre of gravity is privacy and compliance, but with the scope to be involved in wider regulatory, governance and legal use-cases, so comfort and curiosity across these areas is a must.

Because this is a new product vertical for Wordsmith, we're seeking someone who is genuinely excited to build it out from scratch. This is a mid-to-senior role for someone who can work independently and with our Head of Privacy - scoping a problem, building the solution and standing in front of a customer without hand-holding.

What you'll do

  • Build privacy and compliance products — translate messy legal, privacy and compliance requirements into structured, workable solutions that an AI agent can execute.

  • Own the product vertical — shape privacy, compliance and beyond, as a brand new part of the Wordsmith platform, with real autonomy over how it's built.

  • Support pre-sales — sit in front of customers, understand their problems, and build or demonstrate solutions that solve them.

  • Apply the compliance landscape — bring privacy law knowledge and/or the wider regulatory, governanance and compliance landscape, (eg Financial Services compliance or AI Governance), to real customer problems.

  • Extend into general legal work — build more general legal products when the work calls for it, beyond the core privacy and compliance focus.

  • Build with AI, not code — use Wordsmith's own platform to build solutions, with no coding required, but a confident, hands-on understanding of what today's AI can and can't do.


What we're looking for

  • Deep privacy and compliance knowledge, with a strong command of privacy law and/or the wider compliance picture — AI governance, security or specific areas such as financial regulation or employment law.

  • Either a qualified lawyer or a privacy/compliance specialist with real depth in the field, comfortable working across adjacent legal areas when the work calls for it.

  • Strong AI literacy — comfortable using and reasoning about AI tools day to day, with a clear understanding of what today's AI can and can't do, and able to build with it.

  • A builder's mindset — able to take a messy legal, privacy or compliance requirement and turn it into something structured and workable.

  • Client-facing confidence — able to sit in front of customers, understand their legal and compliance problems, and build or demonstrate solutions, including in pre- and post-sales settings.

  • Several years of experience in privacy law or compliance practice, ideally at a mid-to-senior level, with the proactivity to work independently.


Desirable, but not essential

  • Experience in legal tech, RegTech or a SaaS environment.

  • Breadth across the compliance landscape, such as security frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2), AI governance regimes (EU AI Act) or broader GRC.

  • Awareness of, or exposure to, broader legal practice beyond privacy and compliance.

  • Some hands-on building experience — prompt design, workflow automation, low-code tools or similar.

How we work

We're an in-person team based in Edinburgh or London. You should expect to work from the office as your default.

We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. You'll work closely with Sales, Product and Engineering as you build this vertical, with the autonomy to scope your own problems and build your own solutions.

Why Wordsmith

You'll be the first person building out privacy, compliance and regulatory as a product vertical at Wordsmith — a ground-floor opportunity to shape it from scratch, at one of the defining companies in legal AI.

Because we're building in a new technical category, the problems are interesting and genuinely unsolved. You'll have real autonomy over how this part of the platform is built, and the opportunity to grow it as it scales.

Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

Meet the team behind this journey

As a Senior Product Designer at DeepL, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the translation experience at the heart of DeepL Translate, the AI-first translation platform millions of people reach for every day to localize their content. You'll join a cross-functional team that is central to delivering a fast, trustworthy, and scalable product, collaborating closely with product managers and engineering leaders to define and drive the product vision.

Beyond your immediate team, you will actively contribute to DeepL's broader design community—helping evolve our craft, influence best practices, and raise the bar for design across the company.

You will be responsible for solving a critical problem: making translation feel effortless and trustworthy for anyone who needs to communicate across languages — whether they're translating a sentence, a document, or their daily work. We expect you to:

  • You are confident owning and co-owning design artefacts in Figma

  • You have experience working on a product at scale with a global presence

  • You have strong communication and presentation skills

  • You are fluent in English. Any other languages, e.g. German, are an advantage

What we offer

  • Diverse and internationally distributed team: joining our team means becoming part of a large, global community with people of more than 90 nationalities. We're more than just colleagues; we're a group of professionals with a shared mission to connect diverse cultures. Our global presence is growing–we've doubled in size nearly every year, with our employees based in the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, the US, and Japan, and we continue to expand our network.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: as a language-focused company, we value the importance of clear, honest communication. We value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Hybrid work, flexible hours: we offer a hybrid work schedule, with team members coming into the office twice a week. This allows you to engage directly with your team and experience the unique energy of our workspace, while still enjoying the flexibility and comfort of working from home. With flexible working hours and trust in your productivity, we are in sync with your team’s general locations and time zones to foster effective and seamless collaboration.

  • Regular in-person team events: we bond over vibrant events that are as unique as our team, from local team and business unit gatherings, to new-joiner onboardings, to company-wide events that bring us all together–literally.

  • 30 days of annual leave: we value your peace of mind. With 30 days off (excluding public holidays) and access to mental health resources, we make sure you're as strong mentally as you are professionally.

  • Competitive benefits: just as our team spans the globe, so does our benefits package. We've crafted it to reflect the diversity of our team and tailored it to align with your unique location, to ensure you feel supported every step of the way.

If this role and our mission resonate with you, but you're hesitant because you don't check all the boxes, don't let that hold you back. At DeepL, it's all about the value you bring and the growth we can foster together. Go ahead, apply—let's discover your potential together. We can't wait to meet you!

We are an equal opportunity employer

You are welcome at DeepL for who you are - we appreciate authenticity here. Our product is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all succeed, contribute, and think forward! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our diversity that we will find the power to break down language barriers in the world.

About MUBI

MUBI is a global streaming service, production company and film distributor dedicated to elevating great cinema. To make this possible, we create, curate, acquire and champion visionary films, bringing them to audiences all over the world. We have a team of brilliant, dedicated and passionate people to help bring our mission to life. From London to New York, Istanbul to Paris, and Berlin to Mexico - we work together to realize MUBI’s vision.

That’s where you come in! Join our global team and help us make great cinema accessible to everyone, everywhere.

About the role

This is a senior, hands-on product role for someone who wants to own a meaningful slice of the MUBI product end-to-end, and is at their best when the problem is still ambiguous.

You’ll own the Audience & Platform Expansion domain - a critical product surface for our next phase of growth. In this role, you will be responsible for building the scalable foundation to drive global subscriber acquisition and pioneer our tiered premium offerings. You’ll own its strategy, its roadmap and its delivery, from a high-level business goal all the way to a shipped, measured feature. The hardest product problems at MUBI cross team and time-zone boundaries, and break down without someone holding the whole picture; this role exists to be that person for one of these domains.

Reporting to our Senior Product Director, this is a senior, individual contributor role. You'll lead through clarity and influence rather than headcount - aligning engineering, design and data scientists around a vision they actually believe in, and mentoring/coaching other, more junior PMs as you go. We care about craft, in the films we champion and in the products we build, so the bar is product excellence and real user impact, not shipping for its own sake.

We work hybrid-remote where we require 3 office days in Soho, London (if you're in commutable distance from London). Our core days are Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday, with the flexibility to use our offices on the remaining two days if you wish.

Where you'll have impact

You'll own a product surface that leadership relies on, translating ambiguous, evolving priorities into a roadmap teams can execute against - and giving the business a crisp, honest read on what's working, what isn't, and what needs a decision. As you build credibility through delivery, you'll set the standard for how product strategy is articulated and defended at MUBI. Concretely, you'll:

  • Translate business goals into clear, actionable product roadmaps, and own the sub-strategy for a specific MUBI area (e.g. onboarding, content/catalogue discovery, monetization, or viewer experience).

  • Guide technical products through the entire lifecycle - from conception, through development, into launch - and iterate after.

  • Partner directly with Engineering, UX/UI Design, Data Science, Marketing, Business Development and Legal to define product requirements and resolve trade-offs.

  • Establish the KPIs and OKRs for your area, and use data-backed insight to iterate quickly and demonstrate measurable impact.

  • Pitch roadmaps to senior leadership to guide resource allocation, and align engineering, design and analytics teams without relying on direct hierarchy.

  • Write narrative strategy memos and present complex visions clearly - to senior leadership and engineering teams alike.

  • Mentor other team members and raise the bar for product thinking around you.

What you'll bring

  • You've spent significant time shipping complex technical products end to end, and you're happiest owning a problem from the messy, ambiguous start rather than picking up a tidy backlog. You bring structure where there is none - a clear strategy, sharp prioritisation, honest measurement - without becoming a source of process for its own sake.

  • You're technically fluent enough to hold your own with strong engineers: you can translate an ML model, a streaming architecture or a latency constraint into a business trade-off a stakeholder can act on, and tell a real architectural limit from a convenient one.

  • You're an excellent communicator who can flex between an engineer and an executive in the same hour, equally comfortable writing a strategy memo and defending it in a leadership review.

  • You lead through influence - aligning people across functions, regions and time zones around work they want to do.

Qualifications & Expectations

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Design, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 8+ years in product management or a closely related technical role, with at least 3–5 years focused on shipping complex technical products from 0 to 1.

  • Strong business judgment and strategic thinking - able to see the big picture and make connections across teams and issues.

  • Technical acumen: the ability to translate highly technical engineering constraints (machine learning models, streaming architectures, latency) into clear business trade-offs for non-technical stakeholders.

  • Deep domain fluency in identity and access management, subscription management, billing and monetization, and data processing - with the ability to debate architectural and technical trade-offs.

  • A proven ability to lead cross-functional teams through influence rather than direct authority.

Supercell is looking for a Team Support professional to join our London office. As Team Support, you’ll take ownership of the day-to-day support of the office, from travel and team events to the countless practical details that keep things running smoothly.

You’ll be the only Team Support based in London, so this is a role with plenty of independence and responsibility. But you won’t be doing it alone. You’ll be part of an experienced, caring Team Support team across Supercell, with colleagues to learn from and collaborate with. You’ll have the freedom to shape how support works locally, while staying closely connected with your colleagues in Helsinki and collaborating also with other people working with London operations.

At Supercell, independent teams and trust are at the heart of how we work. The same applies to Team Support: you’ll have real ownership of your area and the freedom to decide how best to support the people around you. Most importantly, you’ll have the opportunity to make a visible difference to the experience of everyone working in our London office.

If you enjoy helping people and figuring things out without needing a playbook for everything, you’ll probably feel at home here. Send your CV as well as your application / motivational letter before the application deadline (Thursday, September 17th 2026 9:00 pm BST).

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the day-to-day administrative support for our London office.

  • Coordinate travel arrangements, including flights, accommodation, ground transportation, and the details in between.

  • Plan and organise team days, offsites, internal events, and other moments that bring people together.

  • Help colleagues navigate everyday practical questions, from benefits to general team support.

  • Be a trusted local point of contact for colleagues, leads, and other stakeholders in London.

  • Spot opportunities to improve how things work and take ownership of putting better solutions in place.

  • Confidence working independently and taking responsibility, including in situations where there isn’t an existing process or obvious answer.

  • Strong communication skills in English and the ability to build trusted relationships with people across teams, disciplines, and locations.

  • A collaborative and humble way of working, with a willingness to ask for input, share context, and step in where you can help.

  • You're actively using AI tools in your day-to-day work, and excited about experimenting with new ways AI can improve how we work.

Would Be Nice if You Also Have

  • Experience supporting a growing office or building support practices in an environment that is still evolving.

  • Experience coordinating complex international travel.

Where You'll Be

This role is based in our London studio and is a full-time, permanent position.

Because this role is all about supporting the people and everyday life in the office, we expect you to spend most of your working time onsite in our London office. You’ll also work closely with our Helsinki-based Team Support colleagues and teams whose members are split across London and Helsinki, so expect some travel also between our offices.

–––

That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read.

Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page.

–––

About Supercell

Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars. Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever.

So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And by taking risks, failing, sharing learnings, and killing lots of projects.

Independent cells and trust are at the core of our culture. But it takes more than that to make great games. We take good care of our people, providing them with the compensation, work environment, and resources they need to succeed while having fun along the way.

Benefits and Compensation

Luring you in with glitter, glamour, and gems isn't what we're about. We want you to enjoy your time here fully, so we structure our compensation and benefits with that in mind. It starts with perceiving you as a human being, not a resource.

Not Sure if You Should Apply?

Many candidates with great skills and experience second-guess themselves. The bar is high, but if this role excites you, apply! We’re here to help you succeed. Also, we're happy to learn about any specific accommodations you may need to fully engage in our recruitment process.

Wishing you all the best,
The Supercell Recruitment team

We are establishing a dedicated Compliance Assurance function in the Second Line of Defence, and we are seeking an experienced Entity Assurance Manager to own a single, defensible view of the second-line control environment across Trustly's EU and UK licensed entities.

This role will be part of a community of assurance managers, some of them focussed on specific compliance domains (such as Financial Crimes Prevention, Safeguarding, Consumer Protection, and ICT and Resilience) and some focussed on other Trustly regulated entities. As the Entity Assurance Manager, you own managing the assurance function at an entity level including understanding local requirements, what local regulators expect to see, how findings reach the entity Board and local management team, and what the entity Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) can credibly attest to.

You will confirm the local applicability of domain testing scope and technique, agree the reports that reach the entity Board, and serve as a primary point of contact for assurance matters toward the relevant EU and UK regulators/supervisors. You will work alongside domain assurance managers, Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), and Internal Audit, ensuring that assurance over Trustly's compliance controls is evidenced consistently.

This role is suited to a seasoned assurance, compliance, or second-line risk professional with experience in regulated financial institutions and a firm grasp of the independence boundaries that keep assurance credible.

What you'll do

  • Own a single, defensible view of the second-line control environment across Trustly's EU and UK licensed entities, ensuring that assurance results are comparable, aggregated consistently, and mapped to the ERM risk taxonomy.

  • Confirm the local regulatory applicability of domain testing scope and methodology, agreeing which requirements bite in each EU and UK entity and how findings are rated and reported locally.

  • Own the entity assurance opinion and the reporting of findings to the entity Board and local management team, and support what the entity CCO attests to.

  • Contribute to the annual assurance plan and the single master testing plan through the assurance forum, jointly reviewing and signing off scope with the relevant domain assurance managers before testing commences, to prevent duplicate or gapped coverage.

  • Serve as a primary point of contact toward the relevant EU and UK regulators/supervisors on assurance matters, representing the function credibly and building productive relationships with regulatory authorities.

  • Maintain a disciplined independence boundary by providing independent oversight only.

  • Track findings within the single, unified approach, using the shared issue taxonomy and closure criteria that align with Internal Audit standards.

  • Support Internal Audit's reliance assessment by maintaining a transparent, evidenced audit trail per test, and document any risk-accepted changes to testing cadence.

  • Contribute to standardized reporting, including Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) tracking control health, issue aging, and remediation progress across the entity axis.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Demonstrable experience in compliance assurance, second-line risk, or a related control function within a FinTech, payments, or adjacent regulated financial services environment, with experience in the payments sector preferred.

  • Experience engaging with EU and/or UK financial supervisory authorities, with the ability to represent an assurance or compliance function credibly toward regulators and build productive relationships with them.

  • Sound understanding of the EU and UK regulatory landscape relevant to payment and e-money institutions, including areas such as financial crime, safeguarding, consumer protection, and operational resilience.

  • Proven ability to lead end-to-end assurance reviews, from planning and scoping through to reporting and issue validation.

  • A firm grasp of the three-lines model and the independence boundary between second and third line, with the judgement to keep assurance independent and out of first-line operational activity.

  • Advanced knowledge of control testing methodologies, sampling, issue rating, and evidence standards, and the ability to connect control failures to the firm's risk taxonomy and appetite.

  • Experience working with GRC platforms and unified issue registers, with high attention to detail in the preparation of control findings and management-level documentation.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships across business teams, and to advise and collaborate with stakeholders at various levels, including senior management and Board members.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain complex concepts to non-specialist stakeholders and present to senior leadership, Boards, and regulators.

  • Willingness to work flexibly to collaborate with team members across different time zones.

Shape Your Role and Make an Impact

About ExTrac

ExTrac is a decision intelligence company used by governments, defence organisations, financial institutions, and corporates operating in complex, fast-moving environments. Our capabilities fuse curated data sources, domain-specific AI, and deep human expertise to transform information overload into clear, actionable foresight.

The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is a core region for ExTrac's intelligence coverage, spanning the political and security dynamics, actors, movements, and online ecosystems that shape risk across the region and beyond it. We are the analytical backbone for decision-making when geopolitical uncertainty becomes an opportunity or a strategic risk. More at extrac.ai.

The Role

As a Senior Analyst covering the MENA region, you will help ExTrac understand and anticipate political and security developments across the region, including the activities of state and non-state actors, violent extremist organisations (VEOs), and the online ecosystems in which they operate. Working in Arabic every day, across standard and dialectal material, you will turn what you find into timely reporting that feeds ExTrac's intelligence products and data platform.

What the job involves

Intelligence collection and analysis

  • Monitor and assess political, security, and socio-economic developments across MENA, including regional diplomacy, state and non-state actors, and geopolitical risk, with the ability to contribute to wider global coverage when required.

  • Conduct daily monitoring of Arabic- and English-language media, including news outlets, social media platforms, official statements, and other open-source information environments.

  • Track VEO and non-state armed group activity, including organisational developments, propaganda and communications activity, governance dynamics, operational activity, and regional linkages.

  • Identify new narratives, actors, platforms, and threats appearing across online ecosystems.

  • Apply structured analytical techniques to assess complex information and identify patterns and relationships.

Intelligence production

  • Lead and contribute to daily, weekly, monthly, flash, and deep-dive analytical reporting, with a particular focus on MENA and VEOs.

  • Translate and assess Arabic-language documents and other source material.

  • Contribute to client-facing discussions, briefings, and ad hoc research requests as required.

  • Develop and maintain subject-matter expertise across designated countries, actors, organisations, and thematic areas.

Data curation

  • Lead and contribute to source coverage for the region, identifying and proposing new actors, entities, channels, and outlets for inclusion in ExTrac's research ecosystem.

  • Verify and assess sources in the original language prior to inclusion.

  • Maintain coverage against intelligence requirements, identifying where it should expand or deepen.

  • Contribute to the taxonomy and tagging decisions that structure MENA and violent extremism data.

  • Work with the wider research and data teams to translate analytical judgement into structured data that others can rely on without further verification.

Leadership and collaboration

  • Support the Team Lead with the reviewing, and quality assurance of analytical outputs.

  • Mentor junior analysts on research methodology, analytical standards, and source validation.

  • Support other teams across ExTrac on projects and deliverables when required.

Innovation and capability development

  • Help develop research methodologies, monitoring frameworks, and analytical processes to improve team efficiency and product quality.

  • Integrate AI systems and AI-assisted workflows into analytical practice where they create genuine improvements.

You should apply if

  • MENA is the region you already follow closely, across its politics, security dynamics, and the violent extremist movements and online ecosystems operating within it. This is the region you want to go deeper on rather than a rotation on the way to something else.

  • You work in Arabic, not just alongside it. You read Modern Standard Arabic and dialect comfortably, you notice when slang is doing something new, and you can tell the difference between a shift in language and a shift in intent.

  • Writing is one of your strengths. You can turn a fast-moving, ambiguous picture into a concise, evidence-based assessment under deadline, and you take pride in doing it well.

  • You care about the quality of the underlying data as much as the quality of the analysis built on it, and you hold both to the same standard.

  • You want to keep producing analysis at volume and take on more alongside it. Reviewing others' work, helping set priorities for a small team, and mentoring junior analysts appeal to you as additions to the writing, not a step away from it.

  • You thrive on operational tempo. Daily and flash reporting alongside longer deep dives suits how you like to work, and the pace energises rather than drains you.

  • You are already using AI in your workflow and are interested in what it changes about analytical craft.

Where this role can take you

  • Build recognised subject-matter expertise across your assigned countries, actors, and thematic areas, and take on broader analytical scope as it deepens.

  • Build leadership experience through mentoring junior analysts, quality-assuring their work, and supporting prioritisation across a small team.

  • Support the development of the monitoring frameworks and analytical methodologies used across the team.

  • Shape how AI changes intelligence work itself, championing new tools and methodologies across the Research & Analysis team and influencing how the whole function operates.

Requirements

  • At least five years of professional experience in intelligence analysis, geopolitical risk, disinformation analysis, strategic communications, international security, international relations, or a related field.

  • Strong subject-matter knowledge of the MENA region, including its key political and security actors and regional dynamics.

  • A working understanding of VEOs, their online ecosystems, communications strategies, narratives, and operational activity, built through direct analytical experience.

  • Fluency in written Arabic, across both Modern Standard Arabic and local dialects, including knowledge of slang, with the ability to monitor, analyse, and translate Arabic-language content from a range of sources.

  • Demonstrable experience applying structured analytical methodologies to complex information environments and online ecosystems, including OSINT, network analysis, narrative analysis, sentiment analysis, or other quantitative and qualitative approaches.

  • Strong written communication skills, with a track record of producing concise, high-quality, policy-relevant intelligence and analytical outputs under tight deadlines.

  • Hands-on experience curating source coverage: identifying and verifying online sources, assessing their affiliation, and maintaining structured datasets to a defined standard.

  • Experience proofreading, editing, and quality-assuring analytical products.

  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to work independently while managing multiple concurrent workstreams and competing priorities.

  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to distinguish meaningful developments from high-volume information flows.

  • Able to communicate complex political, security, and extremist-related developments clearly to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.

  • Comfortable integrating AI systems into your workflow to improve outputs and efficiency.

  • A strong understanding of the legal and ethical considerations surrounding intelligence collection, open-source research, and data handling, including responsible use of publicly available information.

Desirable

  • Experience leading analysis on international security, violent extremism, terrorism, or state- and non-state-aligned influence and disinformation ecosystems.

  • Demonstrable experience researching VEOs and extremist online activity, including monitoring affiliated media operations, narratives, actors, and various platforms, such as Telegram, Facebook, Instagram, RocketChat, TikTok, and others.

  • Experience with data science, AI-enabled research tools, or advanced OSINT platforms.

  • Proficiency in one or more additional relevant languages, such as French, Farsi, Turkish, Kurdish, or Russian.

  • Familiarity with the PHIA Yardstick.

  • Experience developing analytical methodologies, research frameworks, monitoring requirements, or data schemas and taxonomies.

  • Experience mentoring junior analysts, reviewing analytical outputs, or leading small analytical projects.

Interview Process

We aim to ensure that each person who interviews with our team has the opportunity to showcase their experience and strengths, and to have honest conversations about whether ExTrac and the role align with their career aspirations. The process for this role is as follows:

  • Initial interview with the hiring manager – 30 minutes

  • Technical craft assessment – two tasks covering analytical writing and source curation, returned within 24 hours

  • Competency-based interview – 45 minutes

  • Senior Executive interview – 45 minutes

Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on skills and experience.

  • A generous benefits package, including Private Medical Health Insurance and an enhanced pension package

  • £500/year education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • 33 days of leave across the year inclusive of bank holidays.

  • A role that combines mission-driven purpose with cutting-edge technology in a fast-growing company.

ExTrac AI provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

ExTrac AI is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing open role within our organisation. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position but all hiring decisions will be made by a member of our team.

Compensation: £58K – £63K

We're looking for a Senior Account Executive to own full-cycle new-logo revenue for Cytix's biggest and most complex deals, in a market where most of the people you're calling haven't heard of us yet. You'll be selling a product, not a service, into CISOs, security engineers and AppSec leads who are used to being pitched by categories they already understand.

Your job is to earn a conversation with almost no brand recognition behind you, then run a genuinely consultative sale that gets underneath what a prospect is actually trying to achieve, not just what they say they want.

You'll take on enterprise and partner-adjacent opportunities, competitive procurement, and buying groups that span security, engineering and the economic buyer. You'll also set the bar for the wider sales team: shaping how SDR intake and Customer Success handoff work, and helping newer Account Executives find their feet.

What you'll do

  • Own full-cycle new-logo opportunities from first qualified meeting through discovery, technical

  • evaluation and signature, sourced by SDR, Marketing, partners and your own prospecting.

  • Self-source a meaningful share of your own pipeline; build an account plan from a cold list rather than relying on inbound or SDR support.

  • Run multi-threaded discovery across security, engineering and economic buyers, uncovering pain that a single conversation would miss.

  • Own commercial negotiation, procurement and security review through to signature, including

  • competitive processes, without needing support from the CRO.

  • Maintain an accurate weekly forecast, with commit-to-close accuracy within 10%, sustained over multiple quarters.

  • Shape SDR intake criteria and the Customer Success handoff standard; informally mentor newer Account Executives on deal strategy and technical positioning.

  • Hand off cleanly to Customer Success at close, with deal-stage commitments documented in the CRM.

What you'll bring

  • 5–7+ years' full-cycle closing experience in B2B SaaS, ideally selling a technical product, not a service, into security or engineering buyers.

  • A demonstrable track record of carrying and hitting quota of £750k–£1m+, at or above 100% in at least two of the last three years.

  • Genuine consultative selling skill: comfortable asking why before pitching how, and building a business case from first principles rather than a script.

  • Confidence selling into accounts where Cytix has little or no existing brand presence, building

  • credibility through the conversation itself rather than a logo slide.

  • A track record of pushing through setbacks and coming back stronger, and of actively seeking out the harder, less familiar deals rather than waiting to be asked.

  • Genuinely bright and inquisitive: you ask sharp questions, pick things up fast, and enjoy getting to the

  • bottom of a problem, whether that's a prospect's business or how Cytix's product works under the hood.

  • Drawn to a business where new challenges show up daily; you take ownership of them and lean in, rather than waiting for someone else to sort it out.

  • Comfortable taking yourself out of your comfort zone: new deal types, new buyer personas, situations you haven't fully rehearsed.

What you'll get

  • Unlimited Holidays!

  • Share options - If Cytix wins, you should too.

  • Enhanced maternity pay.

  • Pension - 8% (3% employer, 5% employee)

  • Private Healthcare (inc. dental, optical and hearing)

  • Octopus car scheme - Drive electric through salary sacrifice

  • Dog-friendly office.

  • Inclusivity as standard - A team where you can do your best work as yourself, no asterisks.

About Cytix

  • Software never stops changing. Teams ship new code every day, through tickets, pull requests, releases, and increasingly with AI in the mix, but the way security keeps up with all that change hasn't really moved on. That's the problem we're solving. Cytix helps organisations understand which software changes actually matter, what should happen next, and how to prove the right call was made. Security understood, in other words.

    We're a small team with big plans, so every person we hire genuinely shapes what Cytix becomes. That's why we're upfront about our five values: we interview for all of them, and they matter to us more than a perfect CV. They're things you do, not things you are, so have a read and see if they sound like you.

     

    Make the first move. When the goal is clear but the path isn't, you get moving rather than waiting for perfect instructions. If you're blocked, you make a sensible call, say what you're assuming, and explain how you'd course-correct. We'd rather you act and be slightly wrong than sit still.

     

    Find the smarter path. You ask why before how. You dig into what the real problem is instead of just building what the spec says, and you're happy to question 'that's how it's always been done' when the reason behind it has gone stale.

     

    See it through. When something's yours, it lands. No loose ends, no surprises for whoever picks it up next. You keep people posted when things change, and if something falls between roles, you catch it.

     

    Raise the bar. You do the best job possible in the time you've got, whether that's a day or a month. Sometimes that means deep craft; sometimes the smartest move is quick and scrappy. It's about good judgement, and we hold each other to it without blame or politics.

     

    Play to win. You care about the mission but don't take yourself too seriously. You say 'I' when things go wrong and 'we' when they go right, trust teammates to do things their own way, and bring a bit of humour when the pressure's on.

Compensation: £75K – £95K • OTE - uncapped 50/50

Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup based in London, founded by Guy Podjarny, who previously founded Snyk. We’ve raised more than $100 million from world-class investors, including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart. In 2025, Tessl ranked #2 in Sifted’s B2B SaaS Rising 100 and #20 in its AI 100.

We’re building the context layer for AI coding agents and a platform for AI-native software development. As an early member of the team, you’ll help shape how we build and scale a company operating at the forefront of AI and software development.

Overview of Role

We're looking for a Developer Advocate to be Tessl's voice in the AI developer community — based in our London office and out in the world where developers actually are. Someone who lives and breathes agentic coding, builds real things with Tessl, and helps other developers do the same.

This is a hands-on, high-visibility role. You'll build with the product, create content people genuinely use, speak at events, and be a familiar face across the communities where AI development is being figured out in real time. You'd rather ship a slick integration or a creative app than just write about one.

A big part of this role is education. Alongside the community work, you'll help build and grow Tessl Academy — our home for learning AI native development. You'll turn what you know into structured, hands-on learning that scales beyond any single talk or tutorial, and takes developers from curious to genuinely capable with Tessl.

Key Responsibilities

Build with Tessl: Go beyond writing about the product, build with it. Create apps, integrations, and creative projects using Tessl that inspire and enable the developer community to do the same.

Teach through Tessl Academy: Design and deliver structured learning, including courses, hands-on labs, guided projects, and certification paths, through Tessl Academy that take developers from their first agentic build to real fluency. Own the curriculum, keep it current as the product evolves, and pay attention to what actually helps people learn, not just what looks good on a syllabus.

Content Creation: Write articles, tutorials, and guides, and produce videos that give developers practical, actionable insights into AI native development with Tessl.

Community and Events: Be an active, visible presence in the AI developer community, speaking at events, participating in forums, engaging on social, and helping highlight what developers are building with Tessl.

Ecosystem Exploration: Constantly explore the AI developer tooling landscape, identifying integration opportunities and ways to connect Tessl with the broader ecosystem.

Show Up Where Developers Are: Run webinars, appear on podcasts, and make yourself at home in other people's communities. That means Discord servers, Slack groups, subreddits, newsletters, and anywhere else developers are gathering.

What You'll Need

Already in the conversation: You're an active voice in the AI developer community, on social channels, where AI discussion is happening. You post, reply, spark discussions.

Active at events: You speak at meetups or conferences, engage in developer communities, and have a point of view worth hearing.

A builder's mindset: You get excited about making things. Whether that's a slick integration, a creative app, or an experiment that no one's tried yet, you'd rather ship something than just describe it.

A teacher's instinct: You can break a complex AI topic into clear, progressive steps that meet developers where they are, and you enjoy the craft of helping someone go from lost to confident.

Strong communicator: You can write clearly and engagingly about technical AI topics.

Development skills: You're comfortable enough with code to build and hack on things yourself. You don't need to be a full-time engineer, but you ship.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building developer education, including courses, curriculum, academies, bootcamps, or technical training

  • Experience with open-source communities and contributor ecosystems


We care deeply about the warm, inclusive environment we’re building at Tessl and we value diversity – we welcome applications from those typically underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this role but are not totally sure whether you’re the right person, do apply anyway!

Learn how we think and work

  • On Tessl, The AI Native Development Startup

  • Announcing skills on Tessl: the package manager for agent skills

  • Podcast Episode: The End of Fragmented Agent Context, Guy Podjarny Tessl CEO

About us

Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production.

 

Trusted by Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline, and more. We're an ambitious team of 100+ working at the frontier of AI and have raised $60M in Series C funding from Wellington Management, CRV, Next47 and Y Combinator.

 

The role

As Finance Associate at Encord, you'll own the operational core of our finance function, including: supplier payments, customer invoicing, and month-end reconciliations - ensuring everything runs accurately and on time. You'll partner closely with the wider finance function and cross-functional teams across the business, helping make finance a great partner to the rest of the company. The day-to-day processes are yours to run and improve: where something is manual or unclear, you'll have the real opportunity to make it better. It's a strong fit for someone early in their finance career who takes ownership seriously and wants their work to underpin the teams building tools for multimodal AI.

 

What you'll do

  • Manage day-to-day bookkeeping, accounts payable, VAT returns and accounts receivable.

  • Process employee expense reports and ensure adherence to company policies.

  • Oversee client invoicing and manage billing workflows.

  • Assist with month-end close procedures, bank reconciliations, and general ledger maintenance.

  • Support financial reporting, budgeting, and variance analysis.

  • Collaborate on ad-hoc finance and operational projects as they arise.

 

Who we're looking for

  • Precision in the core. You take pride in managing the transactional heart of the company. You aren't just processing invoices or reconciling accounts; you view accuracy in bookkeeping and compliance as the critical foundation that allows us to move fast and make informed decisions.

  • A builder of systems. You don’t just accept manual processes as status quo. Whether it’s improving expense workflows or refining billing, you look for the "better way" to do things, ensuring our financial systems scale as quickly as our business.

  • Collaborative by nature. You recognize that effective finance isn’t a back-office function—it’s a partner to the business. You’re ready to bridge the gap between financial operations and the cross-functional teams building the tools for multimodal AI.

  • Ready for high-growth ownership. You are early in your finance career, but you crave responsibility. You want a role where your daily output directly supports our growth, and you’re hungry for the professional development that comes from operating in a fast-paced environment.

 

Experience requirements

  • Degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field.

  • 1-2 years of experience in a finance, accounting, or analytical role (tech or startup experience is a plus, but not required).

  • Solid foundational knowledge of bookkeeping, accounts payable/receivable, and invoicing.

  • Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and organizational skills.

  • Proficiency in spreadsheet software and financial tools. An understanding of AI-native finance stacks would be advantageous

  • Proactive mindset with the ability to adapt in a fast-paced, growing environment.

 

Why Encord

  • Competitive salary, commission, and equity in a high-growth startup

  • Strong in-person culture — most of the team works from our London office 4+ days/week

  • 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays

  • Annual learning & development budget

  • Travel for customer visits, events, and conferences across the UK and Europe

  • Company lunches twice a week

  • Monthly socials & bi-annual team offsites

Join a Prestigious Central London Venue

ROLE SUMMARY

As a Kinly AV Senior Technician you will be expected to support the requirements of the company by providing support of AV & VC equipment across the business, leading and taking responsibility for 2nd and 3rd line technical faults.

 

AV team members must be able to quickly adapt to fast-paced changing environments, and schedules. They need to carry themselves well and provide a high-class service both personally and technically. The team will follow a shift pattern based upon a working week between the hours of 07:30 & 21:00 ensuring coverage throughout the period. 

 

IDEAL CANDIDATE

We are seeking a highly proactive individual with a strong grasp of AV/VC technologies as applied in corporate settings. The ideal candidate should hold industry-recognized AV qualifications, be motivated to expand their knowledge through training, and excel in communication.

Presenting oneself professionally with a friendly and outgoing demeanor is essential, coupled with a positive attitude. This person should readily take responsibility for system ownership and upkeep while consistently seek to surpass expectations. Proficiency in administration, computer technology, PC applications, and networking is a must. Experience supporting other blue-chip companies within the AV industry is desirable.

 

ROLE, RESPONSIBILITIES AND, SKILLS

  • Respond to and manage client escalations effectively by maintaining efficient communication between all relevant stakeholders.

  • Daily room checks undertaken at the start/end of the day, such checks will take into consideration room criticality and any known hardware issues etc.

  • Completing paperwork for each job attended.

  • Communicate identified faults in a clear and detailed manner to our helpdesk colleagues and, where appropriate, to client stakeholders.

VIDEO/AUDIO CONFERENCING

SKILLS PROFILE 

  • Knowledge of collaboration platforms such as Polycom, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Google

  • Excellent organizational and time management skills. The nature of this role involves last-minute requests and as such, flexibility is a key attribute.

  • Maturity, especially when under pressure and being able to maintain excellence in Customer Service with clients of all seniority levels.

  • Ability to work well as part of a small team or independently.

What's On Offer?

About ThriveCart:

ThriveCart is a powerful platform used by over 50,000 people worldwide to generate over $5B in sales. Included within the ThriveCart platform is a learning management system (LMS), affiliate management, cart and checkout functionality, making it a top solution for creators, coaches, consultants, and other businesses.

We integrate with everything you use and have a simple, clean UI with numerous features that allow customers to build income from existing traffic and we are the highest-converting cart for online businesses. Our business is growing, profitable, and backed by LTV SaaS Growth Funds, and we are looking to expand our footprint amongst online businesses.

Location:

Hybrid - UK (up to 3 days a week)

Job Overview:

We're looking for an experienced, strategic CRM Manager to lead the next phase of our customer lifecycle and email marketing strategy. As CRM becomes increasingly central to how we engage, retain, and grow our customer base, you'll own the development of a sophisticated strategy that moves beyond campaign-based email to data-driven customer journeys across the full lifecycle.

You'll shape how we communicate with customers from onboarding and activation through engagement, retention, renewal, and win-back — using segmentation, automation, and experimentation to ensure the right message reaches the right customer at the right moment. Retention and churn reduction are a particular focus.

This is a chance to build and evolve a high-impact CRM function, combining strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

Tasks

What Your Work Will Entail:

  • Own and develop the CRM and lifecycle marketing strategy, with a focus on engagement, retention, and churn reduction.
  • Build and optimize customer journeys across onboarding, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, renewal, and win-back.
  • Evolve email as a strategic communication channel, keeping messaging aligned with the business and customer lifecycle.
  • Create customer segments based on behavior, lifecycle stage, product usage, subscription status, and other signals.
  • Design automated lifecycle programs and triggered communications that drive activation, adoption, and retention.
  • Partner with Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and Data to deliver a cohesive customer experience.
  • Run a structured testing program across messaging, cadence, timing, segmentation, offers, and journeys.
  • Use customer and product data to identify churn signals and opportunities for targeted communication.
  • Define and track CRM metrics: activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn, reactivation, and customer lifetime value.
  • Build reporting that connects CRM activity to measurable business outcomes.
  • Improve CRM processes, technology, automation, and data capabilities to support growth.
  • Ensure customer communications meet privacy, consent, and data protection requirements, including GDPR.

Requirements

What You Bring To This Role:

  • Significant experience in CRM, lifecycle, or retention marketing, ideally within a SaaS or subscription business.
  • Track record of building CRM strategy — not just executing email campaigns.
  • Strong understanding of subscription lifecycles and CRM's role in retention and churn reduction.
  • Experience building automated journeys, behavioral triggers, and customer segmentation.
  • Strong grasp of email strategy: deliverability, personalization, experimentation, and optimization.
  • Comfortable using customer, behavioral, and product data to inform decisions.
  • Experience with CRM, marketing automation, and customer engagement platforms.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn performance data into actionable recommendations.
  • Experience collaborating across Product, Customer Success, Marketing, and Data.
  • Commercial mindset — understands how CRM drives retention, lifetime value, and growth.
  • Strong knowledge of GDPR and best practices for customer communications in the UK and Europe.
  • Excellent communication, project management, and stakeholder management skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in a SaaS or technology company operating a recurring subscription model.
  • Experience evolving CRM strategy during a transition to or expansion of subscription-based offerings.
  • Experience with product-led growth, customer activation, or usage-based lifecycle marketing.
  • Experience designing churn-prevention and win-back strategies.
  • Familiarity with CRM platforms and data ecosystems that enable advanced segmentation, personalization, and automation.
  • Experience helping build or mature a CRM/lifecycle function as a company scales.

What Success Looks Like

You'll turn CRM into a strategic growth and retention channel — building a clear lifecycle strategy, more sophisticated segmentation and automation, more relevant customer communications, and measurable programs that increase engagement, strengthen retention, and reduce churn.

Most importantly, you'll help define the next era of customer communication for the business: a CRM approach that is scalable, data-driven, customer-centric, and closely connected to commercial outcomes.

Learn More About ThriveCart:

Our Values are:

  • Commit to Excellence
  • Find a Way
  • Help Each Other
  • Keep Growing

Full-ownership software engineer responsible for building a new system in TypeScript that will replace our existing PHP system, while maintaining the current PHP system throughout the transition. This is not a hand-off role — you take a problem from requirement to production and own it there. You'll work across both stacks, make technical decisions, and be accountable for what you ship.

We expect you to use AI coding tools as a core part of how you work. Not occasionally — daily. Your velocity, code quality, and problem-solving should reflect effective AI tool use. What we care about is judgment: understanding what you ship, making the right decisions, and knowing when to push back on AI output.

This description applies across experience levels (L1–L4). Interview depth and expectations are calibrated to your level.

  • Features from requirements to production: you break them down, build them, ship them, monitor them

  • Building the new TypeScript system that will replace the legacy PHP platform
  • Maintaining and supporting the existing PHP system throughout the transition

What Your Work Will Entail:

1. Feature Development

  • Take feature requests, break them into tasks, estimate, and deliver independently
  • Build the new TypeScript-based system designed to replace our existing PHP platform
  • Maintain and support the current PHP system in parallel, until the new system is fully migrated
  • Write clean, tested, production-ready code that meets team standards
  • Make technical decisions for features and explain trade-offs clearly
  • Monitor your features in production — logs, metrics, alerts
  • Leave the codebase better than you found it (refactor, document, reduce debt)

2. Production Ownership & Incident Response

  • Respond to dev-escalations with urgency — investigate issues, communicate findings, contribute to resolution
  • Participate in incident response: at all levels, you are expected to show up, help investigate, and support resolution

3. Code Quality & Testing

  • Write unit and integration tests as part of feature work, not as an afterthought
  • Participate actively in code reviews — give thoughtful feedback, act on feedback you receive
  • Identify edge cases and risks during planning, not after deployment

4. AI-Augmented Development (Expected, Not Optional)

  • Use AI coding tools daily: code generation, debugging, test writing, exploring unfamiliar parts of the codebase, code review acceleration
  • Your output should be measurably faster because of AI tools
  • You understand everything you ship — AI is an accelerator, not a replacement for judgment
  • L3+: Help teammates develop effective AI workflows; contribute to team standards for AI tool use

Technical Environment

This role requires active, hands-on TypeScript experience and past professional experience with PHP. Hands-on experience integrating payment platforms such as Stripe and PayPal is required.

Early on, you'll ship your first feature to production, understand the core architecture, and get your local development environment set up. Shared rotation (~1 week/month after ramp-up). Critical: 15 min. High: 1 hour.

We’re on a mission to make migration easy.

We started building Marshmallow in 2017. Since then, we’ve grown from 3 to 700+ people, gained unicorn status, raised ~£140M over three funding rounds, turned profitable, insured millions of drivers and lent millions in car loans.

But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones.

To achieve our goals we need incredibly ambitious, commercially driven people who never settle for ‘good enough’. Marshmallowers are hungry for autonomy and ownership, and would rather improve than coast. Everyone raises standards and has an impact, with a focus on collective success over self-interest.

We’ve created an environment where curious, tenacious people win and grow together. If that sounds motivating, this could be the place for you.

The Claims Validation Team
The Claims Validation Team exists to help to defend Marshmallow against fraudulent activity, and to protect the company loss ratio. Fraudulent claims can result in us losing money, which can then result in driving up the premium prices for our honest customers. We’re here to stop that, by making sure that the right claims are reviewed for any policyholder or indemnity related concerns.


What you’ll be doing

  • Reviewing indemnity referrals flagged by our wider claims team, where it has been identified at the point of claim that customers have misrepresented their policy details, and deciding upon the appropriate course of action for the policy and claim

  • Investigating first party claims by communicating with our policyholders by phone and email and conducting follow up investigations

  • Working proactively and efficiently to minimise leakage

  • Contacting customers regarding document requests or any necessary changes to their policy, and providing excellent customer service

  • Collaborating and building strong relationships with both the wider claims and fraud teams

  • Proactively identifying opportunities to improve our processes to help us to protect both the company loss ratio, and our honest customers

Who you are

  • You have an investigative mindset with strong attention to detail and accuracy

  • You are confident in good decision making, and can work efficiently under pressure

  • You have strong communication skills and are comfortable in liaising with other teams from across the business

  • You enjoy working in a high growth environment and are adaptable to change and balancing conflicting priorities

  • You are a self-starter who likes to take ownership

  • You take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience and enjoy interacting with our customers

  • You are tenacious and persistent; knowing when further investigation can lead to positive commercial outcomes for the business

What we're looking for from you

  • A background in fraud or claims/policy validation

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills to be able to effectively communicate with our customers

  • You are really passionate about the customer, and will go the extra mile to offer them the best service

  • Working in a fast-paced scale up means that you have to be adaptable and excited by the prospect of moving fast

  • You enjoy finding solutions to problems you come across rather than waiting on others to do this for you

  • You enjoy taking ownership of your own workload, and proactively highlight any blockers that you or your team may be facing

Perks of the job

  • Bonus scheme designed to reward high performance

  • Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva

  • Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year

  • Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose

  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

  • 4 weeks Work From Anywhere per year

Our process

We break it up into a few stages:

  • Initial call with someone in our Talent Team (30 mins)

  • A skill-based interview where you will discuss your previous experience also with a focus on our values, our culture and your motivations with our Claims Validation Team Lead plus one other team member (1 hour)

We’ll let you know if you’re invited to an interview or not. But, as a small team with a lot of applications to consider, we can’t give personal feedback on each application.

#LI-PT1

Diversity of thought

We know the best ideas come from having different perspectives in the room - and we're committed to hiring fairly, regardless of background, identity or experience. If you see yourself in this role, we'd encourage you to apply.

  • Communicate openly and directly, and with full context.

All while maintaining a hard-earned reputation for craft and quality.

The role:

We're hiring our first Implementation Specialist to own how our customers first experience the product. You'll take new customers from signature to steady state: handle the configuration, run the training, and get every user live and productive across the Metaview agents that they’ve chosen to get started with.

A great implementation sets the whole relationship up for success. Done well, every end user sees value fast and the customer sees clear ROI against their own success criteria.

This is a brand new role, and there's a ton of room to define what great looks like as we build out the function. It's also one of the most hands-on seats in the company for learning how AI actually gets adopted inside a business. You'll see it happen across dozens of companies a year, up close, at a company defining the category.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Run the implementations for our most strategic customers: work through the plan for each new account, drive the setup, keep it on track, and make sure the customer always knows what happens next.

  • Build each customer’s version of Metaview: a lot of this is prompt engineering. You’ll write the instructions that tell Metaview's agents what a great candidate looks like for each role, give the agents context on the company and how it hires, build note templates around the customer's real interview process, and connect Metaview to their ATS and the rest of their stack. You’ll move customers onto the more advanced features once the basics are working.

  • Run the trainings: end user sessions, hiring manager onboarding, custom loom videos. Success is sustained and increasing usage from all users across all parts of the platform.

  • Watch adoption: spot the teams and users who haven't landed and go back in with targeted training or config changes. You're the customer's first call during the onboarding period, and you know when to pull in the rest of the team.

  • Leave things reusable: turn what you build into assets the next implementation can use, and share what you're learning about what makes onboarding land.

You might be:

  • A couple of years into implementation, onboarding or professional services at a B2B SaaS company with a complex, multi-module product.

  • Already working in the ops side of recruitment - you know the tools and the workflows as well as the hiring.

  • A Metaview power user who's already pushing the product further than most of our team.

  • None of these exactly, but you recognise yourself in the next section.

What you bring:

  • Project management. Not necessarily a previous job title, but one of your real strengths. Comfortable running several implementations simultaneously, each at a different stage with its own milestones, dependencies and stakeholders.

  • Product fluency. You like understanding how things work and you're happy in the detail. You'll learn to write a strong ideal candidate profile, work out why a sourcing search is returning the wrong candidates, and teach a hiring manager to get more from an agent. You're comfortable with configuration, integrations, data and prompts, and you use AI on your own work. Metaview experience is a plus, not a requirement.

  • Training and behaviour change. You can take a complex product and break it into pieces someone can actually use, you adjust when the room isn't following, and you know a session went well when people are using the thing a week later rather than when they said thanks.

  • Hospitality. You sweat the experience. Implementations are tailored to what each customer needs rather than running the same script, and you're easy to have on a call.

  • Systems thinking. You instinctively turn a one-off session into something reusable.

What we offer:

  • The best co-workers you’ll ever have, in an environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance.

  • Supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with AI.

  • High compensation, through cash and equity.

  • Your own Ramp card for lunch & dinner whenever you're in the office.

  • WFH & learning allowance to set up your own space, plus expense any books/resources/tools you'll need for your role.

Are you an experienced construction project leader with the commercial acumen to deliver complex infrastructure projects while managing the expectations of lenders, investors and key stakeholders?

We are looking for an experienced Senior Construction Project Manager to fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role across Elgin’s utility-scale solar PV, BESS and co-located PV/BESS projects. The role is focused on leading multidisciplinary project teams within a single Elgin delivery framework, ensuring that finance, legal, engineering, procurement, construction, operations, route-to-market and external adviser inputs are coordinated into one clear project position from late stage development / FID through construction, commissioning, commercial operations and handover to Asset Management. Particular emphasis will be placed on lender, investor, SPV governance and internal delivery interfaces.
 
This role requires significant project and contract management experience, including direct involvement in project finance processes, lender due diligence, conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender reporting, waivers / consents and coordination with lender technical advisers. The successful candidate will need specific experience with FIDIC based Construction Contracts, strong commercial judgement, disciplined contract administration capability and the ability to translate project delivery status into clear funding, governance and decision-making outputs.
 
To be successful in the role, you will have experience representing a client, employer, sponsor or SPV in the delivery of complex infrastructure or renewable energy projects. You will be commercially astute, highly organised, confident leading multidisciplinary project teams through a common governance and delivery framework, and capable of engaging credibly with lenders, investors, advisers, contractors, shareholder forums and senior internal stakeholders.

What you will be do:

  • Fulfil the Client / Employer’s Representative role for allocated projects, ensuring Elgin’s SPV, governance, commercial and contractual obligations are actively managed from FID through COD and handover.
  • Lead project and contract management on project-financed assets, coordinating lender processes including conditions precedent, drawdown evidence, lender technical adviser queries, lender reporting, waivers / consents and funding milestone submissions.
  • Administer and manage high-value EPC, ICP and related project contracts, including notices, variations, claims, payment applications, completion milestones, liquidated damages, defects and close-out obligations.
  • Maintain disciplined project controls across programme, budget, cash flow, risk, actions, decisions and change, ensuring transparent reporting to senior management, SPV governance bodies, lenders and investors.
  • Act as the primary project coordination point between Elgin’s internal project team, finance, legal, procurement, engineering, construction, operations, route-to-market and external advisers, ensuring that all workstreams operate from one integrated delivery plan, one risk position and one set of decision requirements.
  • Lead and manage multidisciplinary internal project teams within Elgin’s agreed delivery framework by setting priorities, clarifying accountabilities, managing dependencies, aligning workstreams to project milestones and escalating decisions in a timely and structured manner.
  • Manage the relationship and reporting cadence with project finance lenders, equity investors, shareholder representatives, lender technical advisers and other key finance-facing stakeholders, including preparing and presenting clear, decision-ready updates for shareholder forums and related governance meetings.
  • Oversee contractor, owner’s engineer and technical adviser interfaces to ensure delivery evidence, technical outputs and contractual positions support Elgin’s funding, governance and employer obligations.
  • Proactively identify commercial, contractual, programme and financing risks, develop mitigation plans and ensure issues are escalated with clear options, recommendations and decision requirements.
  • Support tendering, contract negotiation and commercial strategy by ensuring delivery arrangements are bankable, financeable, contractually robust and aligned with lender / investor expectations.


Your profile

What you will need: 

  • Degree in project management, construction management, engineering, or similar.

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to assess risk versus reward, protect the employer’s position and communicate implications clearly to senior stakeholders.
